title: Field activation readiness matrix and feedback ingestion pipeline for early-access customers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a pragmatic, enforceable readiness matrix plus an automated feedback ingestion pipeline to ensure the first cohort of early-access / lighthouse customers are activated with predictable outcomes and tight feedback loops. This ticket coordinates release notes, support runbooks, instrumentation, and customer-facing comms so Engineering, Support, Sales, and Customer Success can run field activations without firefighting.
background: We have 8 confirmed early-access customers with varied integration timelines and regulatory constraints. Past pilots suffered from unclear handoffs (sales -> success -> eng), missing telemetry on failure modes, and delayed product fixes because feedback either arrived as Slack threads or ad-hoc emails. This initiative standardizes launch readiness gates and collects structured feedback into a central pipeline for faster triage and measurable success signals.
objectives: Define a 6-point readiness matrix (network, security, capacity, telemetry, comms, rollback plan) and apply to each customer
Ship an automated feedback ingestion flow (email/Support ticket/console link -> normalized event -> feedback dashboard + issue creation template)
Coordinate release notes and customer-facing docs with PM, Docs, and Legal so customers get accurate upgrade instructions
Reduce time-to-first-triage on customer issues to under 2 hours during activation windows
Achieve initial activation success (first useful inference) for 75% of the cohort within 10 business days
acceptance_criteria: Readiness matrix template stored in Confluence and filled for all 8 customers
Feedback ingestion pipeline connected: Support mailbox + Help widget + dedicated console button -> feedback events visible in Gaugeboard and Sentry mappings
Support runbook and on-call rotation documented and distributed; escalation paths verified with 2 simulated incidents
Release notes for the activation release published and reviewed by Legal and Security
Telemetry dashboards show the three key signals (activation success, latency regressions, error rate) for each customer within 24 hours of activation start

rollout_plan: Week -2: Readiness matrix completed per customer, release notes draft, runbook draft
Week -1: Dry run with internal beta; telemetry and feedback pipeline validation
Activation Day 0: Go/no-go checklist review call; support on-call engaged
Activation Day 0-3: High-frequency triage window (2-hour SLAs), daily sync calls
Activation Day 4-14: Reduced cadence; monitor alerts and customer feedback; weekly sync
Day 30/60/90: Success review and decision on GA or additional rollout
analytics_signals: Activation success rate: percent of customers with first successful inference within X hours
Mean time to first triage: time from feedback event to triage issue creation
Per-customer token latency 95th percentile vs baseline
Error type distribution for activation window (auth, network, model mismatch)
Feature usage (API endpoints invoked, embeddings vs text gen ratio)
Customer satisfaction: CSAT after first 2 weeks and NPS at 30 days
runbook_snippets: Immediate triage checklist: collect request id, region, model version, exact prompt, API response and headers
Escalation path: Support -> CSM -> ENG on-call -> Product -> Security (if PII/KMS involved)
Temporary rollback: pin customer to previous model + disable experimental features via per-customer flag
Data collection: instruct customer to upload obfuscated logs to secure upload link; include sample curl commands
decisions: Decision 2025-02-12: Use a lightweight JSON schema for feedback events rather than protobufs to speed iteration (trade-off: less strict typing vs faster rollout)
Decision 2025-02-14: Default to per-customer model pinning during activation windows to avoid noisy drift (trade-off: temporary divergence from mainline)
Decision 2025-02-18: Require Legal sign-off for any example payloads shown in public docs; internal runbooks can contain redacted examples
